//: Type-checks the T4 browser journeys. Referenced by the G10 tasks' `Run:` commands as
`npx --yes tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json`, which had no file to read until this one existed.
This is not belt-and-braces on top of `playwright test --list`. The runner transpiles with esbuild,
which strips type-only imports WITHOUT checking them: a `import type { Page } from "@playwright/test"`
naming an export that does not exist gives `tsc` a TS2459 and `--list` exit 0. So `--list` proves the
specs are discoverable and this proves they would compile.
`noEmit` with no `outDir`: nothing here is built, and a stray `dist/` in a test package would be
collected by nothing and cleaned by nobody.
Deliberately standalone rather than extending `frontend/tsconfig.json`: this package installs
Playwright and the compiler and nothing else, precisely so a journey cannot import application code
and test a module instead of the deployed stack (see package.json). Inheriting the frontend's
`paths` would hand it back the ability to resolve those imports.
`DOM` and `DOM.Iterable` are both needed even though this is a Node process: the bodies passed to
`page.evaluate` run in the browser and are type-checked here, and a spread over a `NodeList` needs
`DOM.Iterable`. Without it, journey 03 fails to compile on code that is correct at runtime.
